findings.text: Stage2 range flush is exposed as a range operation that succeeds immediately when the final force write back capability is present, and otherwise performs a leaf only page table walk over the requested interval using a dedicated per entry callback with the table as context.

The flush callback leaves non cacheable entries untouched and reports success, while cacheable entries trigger a point of coherency clean plus invalidate over exactly one granule at the visited level when that memory operation is provided, always reporting success.

Detached stage2 table creation is exposed as an operation taking a table with physical base with level with protection with cache with a flag forcing smallest granularity, returning a pointer to a newly allocated table or an encoded error.

Detached creation requires the physical base to be aligned to the granule for the level, requires protection attributes to be translatable, and requires a zeroed page allocation, with distinct failures for misalignment and exhaustion, and it releases the partial table when the inner walk fails.

Detached creation walks an artificial zero based interval sized to one granule of the requested level starting one level above, using leaf traversal that omits break before make invalidations and maintenance, with caller supplied memory cache and chosen forced granularity.

Per level table expansion need is fixed with level one needing entries per table plus one, level two needing one, and level three needing none, while any other level warns once about bounds and reports an invalid argument failure.

Stage2 split is exposed as a range operation that runs a leaf walk with a split callback using a caller memory cache as context, then issues an inner shareable store barrier before returning the walk outcome.

The split callback ignores entries at the last level and entries without validity, then selects between building a full tree down to smallest granularity when cache occupancy suffices and building a single page fallback otherwise, failing when even one page is unavailable.

Split derives the owning MMU from the cache container plus physical base plus protection from the old entry, builds a detached child for the same level, attempts an atomic break of the old entry, and on success installs a table entry with release visibility, while contention frees the child and signals retry.

Reclaim traversal only processes counted entries, with leaf visits dropping one page reference and table post visits dropping parent plus child references and clearing the parent only when the child reference count equals one, so freed tables are not rewalked, while other visit kinds report invalid argument.
Active priority register count is a power of two derived from the preemption bit count minus five.
Idle interrupt priority value is decimal two hundred fifty five.
Minimum binary point equals eight minus the preemption bit count, and trap group selection is derived from the exception syndrome register coprocessor field being different from eight.

Highest pending list register selection scans only used entries, keeps pending state entries whose group is enabled in the virtual machine control register, retains strictly lower numeric priority candidates, and reports a spurious identifier when no candidate remains.

Highest active priority combines both active priority banks per index, adds thirty two per jointly empty index, otherwise returns accumulated offset plus lowest set bit scaled by minimum binary point, or idle when all banks are empty.

Group zero binary point comes directly from control state, group one aliases to group zero plus one when common binary point is set with an increment limit, otherwise comes directly, and priority to preemption conversion keeps only bits at or above the applicable point with group zero using one more than stored.

Setting active priority converts priority to preemption then to an active bit index and sets that bit in the bank selected by group, while clearing scans bank pairs for the first non empty index and clears the lowest set bit of the lower bank, rescaled to eight bit priority or idle.

Interrupt acknowledge emulation requires group match plus priority mask strictly above candidate plus highest active strictly above candidate preemption, otherwise returns spurious, and on success moves the list register from pending to active, records active priority, and returns the virtual identifier.
Maintenance count bumping increments the end of interrupt count field inside the hypervisor control register.

Deactivate emulation delegates to an inner helper and bumps the maintenance count only when that helper reports lack of handling, while end of interrupt emulation always drops active priority, bumps count when no matching active entry exists except for locality specific interrupts, honors deactivate suppress mode for non local interrupts, and validates group plus preemption match before clearing active state.

Enable, binary point, mask, and control accesses proxy virtual machine control fields, with binary point writes clamped to a minimum and group one writes ignored when common point is requested, and control reads synthesize priority plus identity plus affinity fields from version information with mode bits from control state.

Active priority register accesses dispatch by current group to bank zero versus bank one at fixed indexes zero through three, running priority reports highest active priority, and highest pending reports the highest pending virtual identifier only when its group matches current group otherwise spurious.
Host per CPU state plus hypervisor CPU context plus hypervisor vector exist as per CPU instances.
Nested guest hypervisor control exclusion mask combines trap general exceptions with pointer authentication instructions with pointer authentication keys with fault injection enable.
Emulated timer control derives its status by comparing stored compare value against computed counter value and updating the interrupt status position accordingly for physical and virtual timers.

Hypervisor timer fast handling applies only to hypervisor context reads, serving control plus compare plus count views for physical virtual and hypervisor timers with direct register versus emulated choice dependent on extended hypervisor mode, including offset adjustment when the counter offset feature is absent, then advances past the trapping instruction.

Hypervisor exception return fast handling is skipped for new nested hardware with extended mode or for nested context, accepts user return only with extended mode plus trap general exceptions and accepts hypervisor return by demoting privilege to host equivalent, authenticates pointer signed variants when supported, then installs sanitized status plus return address.

Hypervisor stage one invalidation fast handling applies only to hypervisor context, decodes trapped instruction plus input value, accepts first exception level operations only with extended mode plus trap general exceptions or second exception level operations directly, performs the corresponding invalidation, otherwise requests the slow path.
